test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: An electric pump can fill a tank in 3 hours. Due to a leakage in the tank, it takes 5 (1/4) hours to fill the tank. How much time will this leak take to empty the full tank if water does not get in or out of the tank through any other point during this period?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let filling time **A = 3 hours** and combined time (filling + leak) **B = 21/4 hours**.

Leak empty time = (A × B) ÷ (B − A)

⇒ (3 × 21/4) ÷ (21/4 − 3) = (63/4) ÷ (9/4) = 63 ÷ 9 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 3 hr, Filling + Leakage time = 5(1/4) hr = 21/4 hr.

 
 **Entity** **Time (hr)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 **Pump (P)** 3 21 7 
 **Pump + Leak (P+L)** 21/4 4 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **Pump (P)** = 7 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Pump + Leak (P+L)** = 4 units/hr

⇒ Efficiency of **Leak (L)** = (P+L) − P = 4 − 7 = −3 units/hr (Negative sign indicates emptying)

⇒ Time taken by **Leak** to empty the tank = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Leak

⇒ Time = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **Inlet** fills a tank (positive efficiency), while an **Outlet or Leak** empties it (negative efficiency).

Combined Work Formula

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, the net work done in one hour is (1/x − 1/y).

Emptying Time Calculation

Time to empty = (Filling Time × Combined Time) ÷ (Combined Time − Filling Time).</p
